summary: Maison Passage Open Jaw Explorer is a browser-demoable overseas open-jaw planning app that helps travelers choose one departure country, compare multiple destination countries, and identify the cheapest inbound entry leg and cheapest return exit leg through a bold Grand Tour Ledger premium dossier experience before handing off to live search.
vision: Turn a complex multi-country overseas trip into a collectible Grand Tour Ledger dossier where the traveler can confidently choose how to enter and leave a region before worrying about internal routing.
target_users: Japanese-speaking travelers planning premium overseas trips across multiple countries.
Travelers who want to compare open-jaw entry and exit combinations before booking anything.
Users who prefer a refined, brand-led browsing experience instead of a dense airfare dashboard.
assumptions: The first release may use curated representative airports and deterministic reference pricing instead of live fare inventory.
Displayed fares must be framed honestly as estimates until the user opens a live provider such as Skyscanner.
The MVP intentionally excludes the route between the inbound arrival airport and the return departure airport inside the destination region.
The default language is Japanese and the default displayed currency is JPY.
The next design sprint should materially upgrade the presentation while preserving the existing overseas open-jaw planner logic, flexible outbound month comparison, and stay-window behavior.
The experience should feel like a premium travel dossier rather than a generic luxury landing page or dashboard.
The app should remain usable in one browser session without login.
Travelers often know a target season such as July through September before they know exact dates.
out_of_scope: Automatic internal routing after the user lands in the destination region.
User accounts or shared collaborative editing.
Guaranteed live prices without a future provider integration.
Hotels, visas, exchange rates, or full itinerary planning.

tone: Grand Tour Ledger should feel archival, cinematic, worldly, and assured rather than politely minimal.
Base surfaces should evoke parchment, binding cloth, inked paper, and premium dossier inserts instead of generic luxury website cards.
Use parchment, oxblood, espresso, brass, and near-black as the dominant palette, with any atlas green or stamp red used sparingly.
Typography and labeling should feel like a curated folio with captions, ledger marks, proof stamps, and editorial side notes.
layout_principles: The page should read like a deliberate dossier journey, with each section behaving like a spread, insert, or annotated rail.
The planner atelier and result folio are the operational centerpieces and should feel integrated into the narrative order rather than bolted onto the page.
Evidence cues such as proof strips, annotations, dividers, and method notes should build trust without turning the page into a dashboard.
The section sequence should be explicit and linear rather than interchangeable.
motion: Keep animation restrained and tactile, such as measured reveals, subtle parallax, or folio-like transitions.
Avoid flashy motion, rapid counters, or high-frequency hover effects that break the premium dossier mood.
required_sections: A fixed refined header that begins light and transparent, then gains a readable archival surface on scroll.
A first-viewport cover spread with bold brand framing, concise copy, and a premium dossier mood instead of a generic hero.
A proof strip immediately below the cover spread that surfaces trust cues such as estimate honesty, airport coverage scale, or method notes.
A planner atelier section that contains the full overseas open-jaw planning interface, including exact-date and flexible-window modes.
A result folio section that frames the recommended outbound and return legs, combined estimate, and supporting alternatives as a premium results spread.
A story/method rail that explains the open-jaw logic and the flexible month plus stay-window approach in annotated editorial beats.
An archetypes section with at least three refined travel profiles or planning styles.
A restrained concierge CTA section that feels bespoke rather than sales-heavy.
A footer that closes the dossier with a dark premium tone.

features.name: Grand Tour Ledger Shell
features.description: The home page should establish Maison Passage as a bold premium dossier brand before presenting the interactive planning tool.
must_have: A fixed refined header that gains a subtle archival surface or blur after scroll.
A first-viewport cover spread with strong brand presentation, concise premium copy, and a clear primary CTA.
A proof strip that communicates trust cues such as estimate honesty, airport coverage, or method details.
A restrained concierge CTA section and dark footer that maintain the dossier tone.

features.name: Grand Tour Ledger Narrative Flow
features.description: The page should communicate value through a bold dossier sequence rather than a generic landing-page pattern.
must_have: The primary section order is header, cover spread, proof strip, planner atelier, result folio, story/method rail, archetypes, concierge CTA, and footer.
The planner atelier and result folio feel like the operational heart of the page, not detached utility modules.
The story/method rail explains the open-jaw decision flow and the flexible travel-window method in annotated editorial beats.
Typography, spacing, dividers, captions, and accents feel premium and consistent from cover spread to footer.

features.name: Planner Atelier
features.description: The dossier experience still needs a practical interface for the overseas open-jaw planning flow.
must_have: Departure country selector.
Exact date input for users who already know the outbound day.
Flexible month selection for users who want to compare multiple target months such as July, August, and September.
Flexible stay-length range selection that can search approximate trip lengths such as 26 to 36 days.
Passenger count selector.
Cabin class selector.
A multi-select destination country picker.
A direct-first toggle.
A primary action to compare routes.

features.name: Flexible Travel Window
features.description: The app should support approximate seasonal planning by comparing many possible outbound dates and a flexible return window instead of requiring one exact date.
must_have: A mode that compares multiple selected outbound months.
A stay-length range with separate minimum and maximum day selections.
The planner chooses the cheapest outbound date first, then searches return dates from that outbound date plus the selected stay range.
Results show how many outbound and return dates were compared.
The result explains the outbound month window, return window, and stay range used for the recommendation.

features.name: Representative Airport Coverage
features.description: Before results are shown, the app expands countries into representative airport sets for practical comparison.
must_have: The departure country expands into multiple representative airports when local data exists.
Each destination country expands into inbound and outbound airport candidates.
The departure country cannot also be selected as a destination country.
The UI explains how many airports are being compared.

features.name: Result Folio
features.description: The core result surfaces the cheapest entry leg and cheapest exit leg separately for an overseas open-jaw itinerary.
must_have: A clearly labeled cheapest outbound entry leg.
A clearly labeled cheapest return exit leg.
A combined estimated total and per-person estimate.
Clear explanation that the internal route between arrival and departure airports is excluded.

features.name: Alternatives And Live Search Handoff
features.description: Users should be able to inspect nearby options and then continue into live search without ambiguity.
must_have: Alternative outbound entry options.
Alternative return exit options.
A per-country airport coverage section.
Links for outbound, return, and combined Skyscanner search handoff.
Honest explanation that live search is the source of truth for final fares.

features.name: Estimate Transparency
features.description: Because the MVP uses deterministic reference pricing, the UI should show uncertainty and evidence rather than presenting one number as a final fare.
must_have: Estimated fares are accompanied by a low-to-high reference range.
Each recommended leg shows a confidence label.
Each recommended leg shows the estimate basis, including season, stop assumption, and distance.
A deterministic smoke test verifies price ranges, confidence labels, open-jaw gap notes, and Skyscanner handoff generation.

acceptance_criteria: The home screen follows the Grand Tour Ledger section order: fixed header, cover spread, proof strip, planner atelier, result folio, story/method rail, archetypes, concierge CTA, and footer.
The fixed header remains readable after scroll without losing the premium archival tone.
The first viewport is a true cover spread with bold brand framing, concise copy, and dossier-like presentation rather than a generic hero.
A proof strip appears immediately below the cover spread and surfaces trust cues such as estimate honesty, airport coverage scale, or method framing.
The planner atelier contains the full overseas open-jaw input set, including exact-date mode, flexible month mode, and stay-length range controls.
The result folio appears as the next major spread after planning interaction and frames the recommended entry leg, exit leg, total estimate, range, and confidence metadata.
The story/method rail explains the open-jaw flow and the flexible month plus stay-window method in multiple editorial beats.
The archetypes section presents at least three refined travel profiles or planning styles.
The concierge CTA appears before the footer and feels premium and restrained rather than repetitive.
The user cannot compare routes until departure country, valid date mode inputs, stay length or stay range, and at least one destination country are set.

For a normal input such as Japan departure plus France, United Kingdom, and Germany as destination countries, the app shows a cheapest outbound leg, a cheapest return leg, and a combined estimated total.

For flexible planning, the user can choose multiple target months such as July, August, and September, choose a stay range such as 26 to 36 days, and receive a best outbound date plus a best return date from the derived return window.
Exact-date mode remains available for users with fixed outbound dates and fixed stay lengths.
The flexible result states the compared outbound window, return window, stay range, and compared date counts.
Estimated fares are shown with ranges and confidence labels so deterministic reference prices are not mistaken for final live inventory.
The result explicitly states that the arrival airport and return airport may differ and that the internal route is not included.
The results area contains links for outbound, return, and combined Skyscanner search handoff.
The visual language uses parchment, oxblood, espresso, brass, and near-black cues rather than generic warm-off-white minimalism.
The page works at approximately 390px mobile width and 1280px desktop width without obvious horizontal overflow.
demo_script: Open the app and confirm that the first impression is a Grand Tour Ledger dossier rather than a generic luxury landing page or dense utility dashboard.
Observe the fixed header, then scroll and confirm that it becomes more readable with a subtle archival surface treatment.
Review the cover spread and confirm that the first viewport feels bolder, more cinematic, and more dossier-like than the previous generic premium shell.
Confirm that a proof strip appears directly after the cover spread and communicates trust cues such as estimate honesty, methodology, or airport coverage.
Use the planner atelier to choose Japan as the departure country plus France, United Kingdom, and Germany as destination countries.
Leave the planner in flexible mode with July, August, and September selected, choose a 26 to 36 day stay range, then run the comparison.
Confirm that the result folio shows the cheapest outbound entry leg date, then finds the cheapest return exit leg within the derived return window, with a combined estimate.
Confirm that compared outbound and return date counts, the outbound window, the return window, the stay range, fare ranges, and confidence labels are visible in the result folio.
Review the story/method rail and confirm that the open-jaw value proposition and flexible travel-window logic are explained in annotated editorial beats.
Review the archetypes section and confirm that at least three premium travel profiles or planning styles are shown.
Confirm that the result explains the open-jaw assumption, excludes internal travel, and retains outbound, return, and combined Skyscanner handoff links.

sprints.name: Open Jaw Planning MVP
sprints.goal: Create the first runnable overseas open-jaw planning app that compares the cheapest inbound and outbound flight legs using local estimation logic.
scope: Build the single-page planning experience in build/.
Expand countries into representative airport sets.
Generate cheapest outbound and return legs from local estimation logic.
Provide alternative route options and Skyscanner handoff links.
acceptance_criteria: A local user can run the app from build/ and compare outbound and return legs in one browser session.
The app does not pretend that deterministic reference prices are final live inventory.

sprints.name: Luxury Editorial Shell
sprints.goal: Wrap the existing overseas open-jaw planner in a luxury editorial brand experience without breaking the planning flow.
scope: Add the fixed transparent header, full-screen hero, concept intro, value collage, alternating story section, lineup cards, restrained CTA, and dark footer.
Adapt the planner and results styling to the warm off-white, gold, bronze, dark brown, and near-black direction.
Preserve the existing open-jaw comparison flow while improving pacing, tone, and visual cohesion.
acceptance_criteria: The page feels like a premium travel brand landing experience from top to bottom.
All required editorial sections are implemented without breaking the core comparison workflow.
All top-level design acceptance criteria are satisfied.

sprints.name: Fare Estimate Integrity
sprints.goal: Make deterministic reference fares more transparent and evaluation-ready before adding a live provider.
scope: Add price ranges and confidence labels to route estimates.
Explain the estimate basis for each recommended flight leg.
Add deterministic planner smoke validation for estimate fields, open-jaw gap notes, and Skyscanner handoff links.
Keep live provider integration out of scope until an API key and provider contract are selected.
acceptance_criteria: The app shows fare ranges and confidence labels for the total and recommended flight legs.
The planner smoke test validates deterministic estimates and handoff links without browser automation.
The Next.js production build works in the local Codex environment.

sprints.name: Flexible Travel Window
sprints.goal: Let travelers compare approximate month ranges and flexible trip lengths before committing to exact dates.
scope: Add a flexible date mode for multiple target outbound months.
Add a stay-length range for approximate trip lengths.
Search the cheapest outbound date first, then evaluate return dates from the selected stay range.
Surface the compared windows and date counts in the result UI.
Keep exact-date mode available for users with fixed dates.
acceptance_criteria: The default planner can compare July, August, and September as target outbound months.
A 26 to 36 day stay range produces a return search window from the selected best outbound date.
The result shows the outbound window, return window, stay range, and compared date counts.
Exact-date mode still works for users with fixed dates.

sprints.name: Grand Tour Ledger Redesign
sprints.goal: Recast the current Maison Passage experience as a bold Grand Tour Ledger premium dossier without changing the underlying overseas open-jaw planner behavior.
scope: Replace the current generic premium shell with the new section order: header, cover spread, proof strip, planner atelier, result folio, story/method rail, archetypes, concierge CTA, and footer.
Upgrade the visual language to a bolder dossier system using parchment, oxblood, espresso, brass, and near-black cues.
Preserve the existing planner behavior, including exact-date mode, flexible month comparison, stay-window search, estimate transparency, alternatives, airport coverage, and Skyscanner handoff links.
Reframe the copy and information hierarchy so the planner atelier and result folio feel like the operational centerpieces of the page.
acceptance_criteria: The page follows the full Grand Tour Ledger section order with clear, intentional pacing.
The redesign feels materially bolder and less generic than the prior luxury editorial shell.
The overseas open-jaw planner, flexible months, stay-window behavior, range labels, confidence labels, and handoff links remain intact after the redesign.
The planner atelier and result folio are visually prominent without regressing mobile or desktop usability.

sprints.name: Live Fare Enrichment
sprints.goal: Introduce a real fare source or provider-backed enrichment after the Grand Tour Ledger redesign lands.
scope: Introduce a live price provider or search integration.
Distinguish clearly between cached estimates and live prices.
Handle provider errors without breaking the planning flow or premium dossier presentation.
acceptance_criteria: The app can show at least one live or near-live fare source for the suggested entry and exit routes.
If the provider fails, the interface explains the fallback honestly.
